1.  Through this application, the Appellant seeks suspension of sentence during the pendency of the present appeal.
2. The Appellant has been convicted by judgement dated 28th May, 2022 and order on sentence dated 6th July, 2022 passed by the ASJ-01 (POCSO), North, Rohini Court.

The said decisions emanate from FIR No. 677/2016 registered under Sections 377/354B/511 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 1 and Section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 20122 at P.S. Jahangir Puri.

1 3.2.
Rigorous imprisonment for 6 years along with payment of INR 1,000/- as fine for the offence under Sections 10 of POCSO Act, in default simple imprisonment of 1 month;
3.3. Rigorous imprisonment for 3 years along with payment of INR 1,000/- as fine for the offence under Section 354B of IPC, in default simple imprisonment of 1 month.
All the sentences are directed to run concurrently.
4. Ms. Inderjeet Sidhu, counsel for the Prosecutrix, on instructions from the Prosecutrix and her mother, states that she has no objection if the Appellant's sentence is suspended.

She, however,
requests that in the event, the Appellant is released, he should not contact the Prosecutrix or interfere in their life.

Additionally, Ms. Sidhu has expressed apprehension that the Appellant, being the father of the Prosecutrix, may insist to reside in the same house where the Prosecutrix and her mother are currently residing.

5. In response, Ms. Sunita Arora, counsel for Appellant states on instructions, that in order to allay the apprehension of the Prosecutrix, the Appellant would reside at Sector 135, Panchil Nagati Vajipur, Bihari Market, Gali No. 16, Bablu Store, Noida, and undertakes not to contact the Prosecutrix or her mother.
6. The Court has considered the afore-noted facts and submissions.
As per the Nominal Roll, as on 22nd October, 2024, the Appellant had undergone 4 years, 11 months and 10 days.
Further, on 22nd October, 2024, the Petitioner has earned remission of 6 months and 22 days.

Thus, the "POCSO Act"

Thus, as on date, the Appellant has undergone more than 50% of the total sentence.

7. In Sonadhar v. State of Chattisgarh3 and Saudan Singh v. The State of Uttar Pradesh,4 the Supreme Court has observed that in cases other than the ones concerning life sentences, broad parameter of 50% of actual sentence undergone can be the basis of granting bail.

entities.text: Saudan Singh v. The State of Uttar Pradesh,4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8. In Saudan Singh the Supreme Court inter alia held as under:
"7.

We may note that there may be even convicts in custody in cases other than life sentence cases and in those cases again the broad parameter of 50 per cent of the actual sentence undergone can be the basis for grant of bail."

sentences.text: The jail conduct of the Appellant for last one year and overall conduct has been found to be satisfactory.
The hearing of the appeal is likely to take some time.

If the Appellant's sentence is not suspended, there is a possibility that he will serve the entire sentence before his appeal is heard,
rendering the appeal process merely a formality.

10. Considering the aforenoted decisions of the Supreme Court and the fact that the Appellant has undergone nearly 50% of the sentence awarded and since the hearing of the appeal is likely to take some time, the Court is inclined to suspend the sentence of the Appellant during the pendency of the present revision petition.

11. Accordingly, the Appellant shall be released on bail, subject to him furnishing a bail bond in the sum of INR 10,000/- with one surety of the like amount, subject to the satisfaction of the concerned Jail Superintendent/Trial Court/ Duty MM on the following conditions:
